reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: mount 256 effects on one identity and detach all of them — no write, no wake
reading.floor: the same 256 through 3.12.1: subscribeOnKey on one key, then every release called
reading.caveat: WHAT A COMPONENT PAYS TO APPEAR AND LEAVE, with nothing happening in between. This is the half of the churn scenarios that is not a wake, isolated from the adapter, the dataset and the consumer that surround it there. WHY IT IS WORTH ITS OWN ROW: the churn family times mount, wake and unmount as one number per script, so a design that is dearer to mount and cheaper to wake reads as one verdict when it is two [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]. THE DETACH IS INSIDE THE CLOCK ON BOTH ARMS, and it is the part where the two designs differ most: ours splices itself out of every root it filed on, the old one removes a handler from a carrier's list. RESIDUALS. AGAINST US: an `OIMEffect` is born holding its two source lists, stamps itself against the clock and files itself onto every root it reads; the old engine's handler is a function put in a carrier's list. AGAINST THE OLD ENGINE: its subscription is addressed BY A KEY, so `subscribeOnKey` reserves a carrier through the collection's provider — a hash it pays and we do not, because ours is handed the identity itself. THAT ASYMMETRY IS THE DESIGN'S, NOT THE HARNESS'S: 3.12.1 has no slot-addressed subscribe, which is stated in `adapters/oimdb-legacy.ts` where the same limit forces `holdChurnRows` to resolve keys first. WHAT IS ON NEITHER SIDE: any value. No entity is written, no patch is merged, no comparator runs and no derivation is settled, so a row here is the subscription machinery and nothing else. WHAT IS ON BOTH SIDES: one flush per frame, each engine's own.

reading.ours: 256 effects on ONE identity; write it once and flush — every body called
reading.floor: the same through 3.12.1: markUpdatedKey on the key its 256 handlers share, then flush
reading.caveat: THE WAKE, AND NOTHING BUT THE WAKE — the subscriptions are mounted before the clock starts and are never taken down. One identity moves and every subscriber on it must be called exactly once, which is the case where a design either walks a list or dedupes a set. WHAT THE ROW CANNOT SEE: coalescing across a frame. One write per frame means neither engine is asked whether it can be told twice and report once — that is `alt.coalesce-vs-eager.*` in `alternativePairsDispatch.ts`, and it is a different question from this one. reading.ours: 256 effects on 256 identities; write every one and flush once
reading.floor: the same through 3.12.1: markUpdatedKey on all 256 keys, then one flush
reading.caveat: THE OTHER WAKE: a list in which every row moved, so the frame carries as many identities as it does subscribers. READ AGAINST THE ROW ABOVE — the two differ in ONE thing, whether the wakes share an identity, so the pair says whether a design is paying per subscriber or per identity, which a single row cannot [FIGURE STATED IN ADVANCE]. THE OLD ENGINE PAYS A HASH PER MARK HERE and we do not, for the reason under every row of this file: its subscription is keyed and ours is held. That is a difference between the designs and it is exactly what this row is for, but it means the row must not be quoted as "dispatch is faster" without the clause naming what it is faster AT.
